title: Source Ledger Merge: duplicate syllabus rows stop costing quality

ciFast.note: Fast verification is claimed only after v0.15.54 is pushed and the GitHub Actions run is attached.

deploy.note: Pages deploy is not claimed until the pushed release completes its deploy run.

ciDeep.note: This is a narrow exporter/source-ledger truth patch, so focused exporter coverage plus normal local gates are the release bar.

liveProvider.note: The recorded browser smoke is required after commit because it refuses dirty and ahead-of-origin worktrees.

manualHuman.note: No external instructor approval is claimed by this release.

claims.summary: Fresh browser evidence showed weaker syllabus-derived source rows duplicated stronger trusted DOI/URL rows and created avoidable missing-license P2 findings.
Source-ledger bundle merging now dedupes by stable DOI/URL/title identity and keeps the stronger source row when duplicate identities collide.
When a weaker duplicate carries lesson placement evidence, its concept links are merged into the retained stronger source row.
The source-ledger grader remains strict: generic open-access proof is still ambiguous, and this release removes duplicate weak rows rather than hiding findings.

carryForward.next: Improve provider/research retrieval so rows like kr2 receive explicit license metadata or remain honestly flagged for review.
Keep auditing Course FAQ and study-guide outputs for prompt-artifact leakage after the source-ledger duplicate loss is removed.
After v0.15.54 deploys, run a fresh EduTool.dev ZIP/log audit and compare the remaining source-ledger findings against this duplicate-row fix.
